chapter: Touring in the bus years and Jim Crow in the South
title: Melvin Moore's accident, loyalty and later jobs
summary: Kenton admires Melvin; after a fall from a ladder he stays loyal, later working with Millinder and Dizzy Gillespie, and losing the Elliot Lawrence tour.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: I was in New York recording once, I have a picture there, you can have it if you want to, of Stan Kenton--
I have it there.
Yeah, sure enough.
He was there when we were recording and he was flipping over Melvin Moore.

You do know this: The rumors were that Melvin was in part ownership of your band because he was so loyal, he wouldn't leave. I worked in Lucky Millinder's band and all of us said he should have been a big star.
No joke; really.
I think, to tell you the truth, as I said before when we were talking, we were
just too loyal to each other. We were loyal; and then Melvin had an accident.

We were down south, somewhere, once, and Melvin was hanging up a speaker. We didn't have all these extra roadies that we call them now, so what I would do is I would pay him extra for putting it up. He went and slipped off of the ladder and hurt his head, and he had to go in the hospital and I had to leave him there for a while and I paid him just the same and almost hate that I did it, because after then Melvin just knew that he shouldn't leave me.
How long was he in the hospital?
He stayed in the hospital at least a couple of weeks.
In what town?
Somewhere down south.
We were working and we were all sending Melvin money and he came on out and then the funny thing about it, it was pretty serious and I
still had a female vocalist along, Estelle--
Estelle Edwards?
Yeah.

And so, she was kind of helping Melvin, he had to get back to himself, you know, really singing, after that. It looked like Melvin was saying, I just can't do it.

I just hated that I didn't know enough about (inaudible) when they were still after him, because they were after Melvin a long time after that, and so Melvin did--Lucky Millinder--but when he left the band, he went with Diz.
That's right.

And then the big break that he had was with Lawrence Elliot-- Elliot Lawrence and he sent pictures of Melvin, he was going down south, and when he sent pictures of Melvin down there, they told him they had to leave him, and so Elliot Lawrence cancelled the tour; he wouldn't go.

So then Melvin said he always
Estelle Edwards stayed with you a while?
Oh, yes, she went on. Of course Melvin was in the band a long time after that accident, because he got back straight on, way before he got with Diz.
